::: {.callout-note .legacy appearance="simple"}
This post is from the blog I kept as Preceptor in Mathematics at Harvard (2005–2008). It's kept here as an archive; some links are dead and references are dated.
:::

I recently got the inaugural issue of [The Harvard College Mathematics Review](http://www.hcs.harvard.edu/hcmr/index.html).  It’s very nice and obviously took a lot of work

Here’s the list of student articles:

- Dunking Donuts: Culinary Calculations of the Euler Characteristic (Alexander P. Ellis, ‘07)
- Dirichlet’s Prime Number Theorem: Algebraic and Analytic Aspects (Igor Rapinchuk, ‘07)
- Quivers (Virigina Fisher ‘08 et al)
- A Fitness-Based Model for Complex Networks (Zhou Fan ‘10)
- Does Every Polynomial Root have a Simple Approximation? (Bryan Gin-Ge Chen ‘07

Plut there’s an article about the [ABC conjecture](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abc_conjecture) by Prof. [Noam Elkies](http://www.math.harvard.edu/~elkies/), a list of problems, and a nice little anecdote about teacher preparation by [Dennis Gaitsgory](http://www.math.harvard.edu/~gaitsgde/).

And since I’m talking a lot of TeX these days, I’ll say that there are some very nice graphics done in METAPOST by Zachary Abel, ‘10.
